decision: Redesign W1 now around an intermediate human claim, monotonic proposal and target revisions, revision-fenced latest-state projection, and durable reconciliation.
durable_pair_invariants: proposed or failed plus prior target means no human claim owns the mutation
approved plus prior target means one actor owns exact change and snapshot but target is not yet applied
applied, measuring, or active requires the exact applied target revision or an explicit later operator revision
reverted records the exact atomic revert transition; later target revisions are allowed but stale proposal projection is not
reconciliation-required is durable and externally distinguishable when target, proposal, or projection cannot be proven coherent

architecture.proposal_revision: Add a monotonic integer revision/generation to every proposal row/model. Increment it on every SQLite and PostgreSQL status/patch transition. Bind id, source status, and expected revision in every CAS, including forward and inverse atomic scope transactions. Real ABA cycles must reject stale writers.
architecture.target_revision: Add a monotonic agent-config revision suitable for fencing complete profile projections. Increment it on every repository update that can affect the projected profile, including fixed-column scope CAS. Returned rows must carry the committed revision.
architecture.human_scope_claim: For scope mutations, atomically claim proposed/failed into approved, binding a safe actor, exact stored kind/change bytes, expected proposal revision, and a non-null verified v2 snapshot. The direct scope claim primitive must reject omitted, malformed, unbound, legacy, or nullable material at runtime.
architecture.atomic_apply: After the approved claim, atomically CAS the exact target from prior to applied and transition the same proposal revision from approved to applied in one SQLite transaction. PostgreSQL split-store scope apply must refuse before either write. A target CAS miss must leave a recoverable non-applied status.
architecture.projection_fence: Never project a stale returned row. All complete profile writes must use one revision-aware, per-profile serialized/fenced projection boundary and project the latest committed row. A stale expected revision must refuse rather than overwrite a newer projection. File replacement remains atomic. Cross-process behavior must be explicit and tested to the supported deployment contract.
architecture.projection_failure: A blocked, failed, stale, or thrown scope projection cannot advance measurement. If exact atomic inverse of target and proposal succeeds, move to a retryable non-applied state and project the latest row. If inverse or reprojection cannot be proven, durably mark reconciliation-required without overwriting concurrent bytes.
architecture.revert: Atomic target plus proposal revert remains exact-kind/change/snapshot/status/revision-bound. Post-commit projection uses the shared latest-state fence. Ambiguous commit, inverse failure, or stale/failed reprojection becomes durable reconciliation-required, never skipped or a no-change message.
architecture.strict_boundaries: Use strict duplicate-aware raw JSON before every human validator/applier, unattended status change, measurement status change, scope preparation, snapshot verification, and revert. Runtime kind membership is exact; whitespace-normalized unknown kinds are high/refused.
architecture.scope_detection: Aggregate agent-config target and operation evidence across each object/array subtree, including malformed own-property target values and sibling order permutations, while retaining explicit unrelated recipe controls.
architecture.field_semantics: allowedSkillsJson supports arrays only; tools maps are allowed only for allowedMcpsJson. Reject byte changes that are runtime semantic no-ops. Generic refine-config and every non-scope kind must reject protected scope fields instead of emitting legacy snapshots.
architecture.measurement: Measurement of a scope row must strictly parse and validate exact kind/change/snapshot/target/revision before active or revert. Invalid, duplicate, legacy, or ambiguous rows become durable reconciliation-required. Measure outcomes, optimizer summaries, routes, and sweeps preserve that outcome.

criteria.text: Common human validation and all status-changing consumers reject duplicate, malformed, and exact-kind-invalid JSON before side effects.
The shared detector catches malformed target values and target/operation context split across sibling objects or arrays without making unrelated recipe operations high risk.
Protected scope fields cannot flow through generic refine-config or another non-scope applier; allowedSkillsJson rejects object maps and effective no-ops.
Every proposal mutation is revision-CAS-safe in SQLite and PostgreSQL; failed self-loop and measuring-reverted-measuring ABA probes reject stale writers.
A one-winner human scope claim stores actor, exact kind/change, verified v2 snapshot, and source revision in approved before any target or file effect.
Approved-to-applied target mutation is one revision-bound SQLite transaction; target-CAS miss, proposal failure, and PostgreSQL split-store refusal preserve a coherent recoverable pair.
Apply, revert, compensation, and ordinary profile writes share a revision-aware projection fence; both microtask and barrier interleavings leave the file equal to the latest database revision.
Projection failure and commit uncertainty either atomically restore a retryable pair or durably record reconciliation-required, preserving concurrent target bytes.
reconciliation-required propagates through measurement, optimizer summaries, routes, persistence, and retry/recovery selection without becoming skipped/conflict/no-change.
Scope measurement cannot activate duplicate-key, legacy, unbound, stale-revision, or semantically invalid rows.
All prior W1, real HTTP, SQLite/PostgreSQL parity, telemetry overlap, build, diff, and security gates remain green under Node 22.

required_permanent_tests: Production-order human route: prepare, approved claim, atomic target+applied transition, projection, measuring; assert durable pair after each injected failure.
Direct scope claim rejects omitted change, null/legacy/mismatched snapshot, changed stored kind/change, invalid actor, and stale proposal revision.
Real SQLite ABA barriers for failed-to-failed and measuring-to-reverted-to-measuring; PostgreSQL SQL-shape and zero-row parity bind revision.
Microtask and explicit barrier projection races for human apply, revert, inverse/reprojection, and ordinary config writer using a temporary HOME.
Real blocked, failed, stale, and thrown writer outcomes with target/proposal/file assertions.
Strict duplicate human refine-config and strict duplicate measurement rows.
Malformed/null/number agentConfigId and sibling target-operation permutations through detector, classifier, unattended apply, human validation, measurement, and revert.
allowedSkillsJson object-map rejection and valid allowedMcpsJson tools-map control.
Whitespace-padded and unknown exact kinds remain high/refused.
reconciliation-required route, measurement, optimizer-summary, persistence, and sweep behavior.
Real target and proposal BEFORE/AFTER trigger rollback controls.

required: Focused corrective-6 tests show RED before production edits and GREEN after each vertical slice.
Exact 14-file W1 gate plus all new migration/revision/projection/reconciliation tests.
Real ephemeral HTTP route suite outside restricted sandbox if listen is denied.
git diff --check and added-line security scan.
Parent reruns all six reviewer/parent reproducers.
Two fresh independent review lanes inspect the final immutable head.

constraints: No live Rhythm or OpenCode database access or mutation.
Use in-memory SQLite, mocked PostgreSQL, temporary HOME, fixtures, and ephemeral listeners only.
Do not touch W2, W3, or the integration checkout.
No persistent server, external network action, push, PR, merge, or raw sensitive payload logging.
Do not delete prior tests to obtain green counts.
Do not claim acceptance; parent verification and two fresh independent review lanes are mandatory.
